newsitem.title: UK: Rebel Lloyd's Names say they will keep litigating.
newsitem.headline: Rebel Lloyd's Names say they will keep litigating.

text.p: A small group of individual investors in Lloyds of London said on Thursday it will keep up the legal pressure on the insurance market to come up with an improved compensation offer.

The United Names Organisation (UNO) represents some of the Names who have not accepted a 3.2 billion stg compensation offer put together by Lloyd's in respect of the market's 8.0 billion stg plus losses.
"We will be a big thorn in their (Lloyd's) side until the Names who are left get justice," UNO co-chairman David Harris told reporters at a news conference ahead of a meeting later today.
Lloyd's settlement offer has been accepted by 32,294 of Lloyd's 34,000 backers, who in return have agreed to end litigation against those involved in the market.

UNO differs from many of the action groups which sprang up in the the last four years to pursue claims for compensation against particular Lloyd's syndicates and agencies such as Feltrim and Gooda Walker.
It will support legal action against Lloyd's itself on several fronts, co-chairman Catherine Mackenzie-Smith said.
In particular, UNO plans to support the so-called Mason case brought by a Canadian Name alleging that he was not made fully aware of some of the potential claims facing the market when he joined.
This case concerns allegations made by many Names over the years that some market practitioners concealed information about the likely extent of asbestosis related insurance claims.
"Lloyd's deliberately misrepresented the situation, either knowingly or recklessly," Mackenzie-Smith said.
Harris said he was confident that UNO would be able to stop Lloyd's from enforcing writs against the rebel Names who owed money to Lloyd's, but could not or would not pay.

UNO hopes to attract most of the 1,700 or so Names who have not accepted Lloyd's settlement and create a 4.5 million stg litigation fund, Harris said, adding that it had also received offers of financial help from Names who had accepted the deal.
Many of UNO's founders have been involved with other Names' groups, such as the Non American Names Association, and have experience of litigation.
UNO was a force to be reckoned with and would eventually bring Lloyd's back to the negotiating table, Harris said.
One Name supporting UNO told reporters that she could pay her debts to the market, but had not done so as a matter of principle and would "fight Lloyd's to the death."
